sourcedFrom: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH (2023)
cleanIntro: The ShedHorn is a .50 percussion muzzleloader built like a sidelock: a lock plate, a barrel held in the stock by a wedge and a tang screw, a half-cock notch, a double set trigger, and a musket cap on the nipple. Unlike most traditional sidelocks, its Accelerator breech plug comes out of the barrel, and Traditions recommends taking the gun down and cleaning it in detail after every shooting session. The one thing the book forbids outright is taking the bolster drum off the breech plug.

steps.title: Hammer at half cock, and treat it as loaded
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe and put the hammer on half cock before anything else. A muzzleloader has no action to open, so nothing you can see tells you it is empty. You have to prove it with the ramrod.
steps.quote: WARNING: CONFIRM THE SHEDHORN™ IS UNLOADED, UNPRIMED, AND IN THE HALF COCK POSITION BEFORE CONDUCTING ANY OF THE METHODS IN THIS SECTION.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 18. Cleaning & Maintenance, printed p.42

steps.title: Look at the nipple and take off any cap
steps.action: With the hammer at half cock the nipple is uncovered. Look at it. If there is a cap on it, new or fired, lift it off. A live cap on a fouled nipple can go off from a knock, and the hammer is sitting right over it.
steps.quote: 1. Check to be sure the hammer is in the half cock position. 2. Visually inspect the nipple to see if a cap is installed. 3. If a new or spent cap is in place, remove it to de-prime the firearm.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 7. Checking That Your ShedHorn Is Unloaded & Unprimed, printed p.24

steps.title: Run the ramrod down to the breech plug
steps.action: Take the ramrod out of the thimbles and run it down the bore until it stops on the face of the breech plug. On an empty ShedHorn about an inch of rod is left standing above the muzzle.
steps.quote: 1. Remove the ramrod from the thimbles. 2. Insert the ramrod into the barrel. When it is touching the top of the breech plug it should sit approximately 1" above the muzzle.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 7. Checking That Your ShedHorn Is Unloaded & Unprimed, printed p.24

steps.title: Listen for metal on metal. A charged barrel is never cleared by firing
steps.action: When the jag reaches bare steel you should hear it ring. A dull stop means powder, a projectile or something else is down there. Traditions sends you to the disassembly procedure to get it out, with the breech plug removed. You do not shoot it out.
steps.quote: Note: You should hear a metallic sound as the jag makes contact with the breech plug. If you do not hear the metallic sound then the barrel may be either obstructed or charged. To remove the obstruction or the charge, disassemble the firearm following the disassembly procedures outlined in this manual. Do not attempt to clear the barrel by firing.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 7. Checking That Your ShedHorn Is Unloaded & Unprimed, printed p.24

steps.title: Mark the ramrod at the empty depth
steps.action: Once you know the barrel is empty, mark the ramrod permanently where it meets the muzzle. From then on, one push of the rod and a look at the mark tells you whether the gun is empty.
steps.quote: 3. Once you have determined your firearm is unloaded, mark the ramrod with a knife or some sort of instrument that will remain permanent. This will allow you to easily see if your firearm is unloaded in the future.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 7. Checking That Your ShedHorn Is Unloaded & Unprimed, printed p.24

steps.title: Ramrod out, then drift the barrel wedge out from the lock side
steps.action: Take the ramrod out of the thimbles. The barrel wedge goes out through the lock side of the stock. Use a wedge puller, or a non-marring punch and a rubber mallet. A steel punch on the wedge marks both the wedge and the wood.
steps.quote: 2. Remove the ramrod from the thimbles. 3. Carefully remove the barrel wedge from the lock side of the firearm by using a wedge puller or a non-marring punch and rubber mallet.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly, printed p.45

steps.title: Both lock plate screws out. Watch the ramrod spring
steps.action: Back out both lock plate screws with a flat screwdriver. The ramrod retaining spring hangs on the forward screw and comes loose when that screw comes out, so note which way it sat. It has to go back on that screw the same way.
steps.quote: 4. Remove both lock plate screws with a flat head screwdriver. The ramrod retaining spring will be detached from the screw and will require re-installation upon reassembly.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly, printed p.45

steps.title: Tang screw out
steps.action: Take the tang screw all the way out and put it somewhere safe. If it is still in, the barrel cannot come away from the tang. Forcing it is how tangs get bent.
steps.quote: 5. Remove the tang screw with a flat head screwdriver. Set aside.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly, printed p.45

steps.title: Lift the barrel slightly, then draw it straight out
steps.action: Raise the barrel only a little, then pull it straight forward out of the stock. A slight twist helps it clear the tang. Lifting hard, or pulling with the tang screw still in, levers on the tang and can bend or break it.
steps.quote: 6. Lift the barrel up slightly and then pull it straight out of the stock. You may need to twist the barrel slightly to pull the barrel away from the tang. If the tang screw is not removed or if there is too much upward pressure when lifting the barrel, this can bend or break the tang.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly, printed p.45
steps.warn: IMPROPER REMOVAL OF THE BARREL WILL DAMAGE THE TANG AND IS NOT COVERED UNDER WARRANTY.

steps.title: Unscrew the breech plug counter-clockwise
steps.action: Hold the barrel in one hand and turn the breech plug counter-clockwise with the other. On the ShedHorn this is a routine step, not a gunsmith job. The plug is built to come out, and that is how the bore gets cleaned from the breech end.
steps.quote: 7. Grasp the barrel in one hand and use the other hand to rotate the breech plug counter clockwise to remove from the barrel.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly, printed p.46

steps.title: If the plug will not turn by hand
steps.action: Clamp the barrel in a padded vise and turn the plug out with a 6 mm Allen wrench in the hex socket in its back. The other option is penetrating oil down the muzzle, left for an hour. A plug that fights you is usually fouled or under-greased threads. That is why the threads get greased every time it goes back in.
steps.quote: A. Place the barrel in a padded vice to allow for better leverage and use a 6mm Allen wrench to remove the breech plug. Insert the post of the wrench into the hex socket in the back of the breech plug and turn the handle counter clockwise. OR B. Spray penetrating oil down the muzzle of the barrel and let sit for one hour.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly, printed p.46

steps.title: The bolster drum stays on the breech plug
steps.action: The plug comes out of the barrel, but the bolster drum does not come off the plug. Traditions forbids it in plain words, three times in this book. Clean the drum's channel through the clean-out screw hole instead. That is the access the maker provides.
steps.quote: DANGER: NEVER REMOVE THE BOLSTER DRUM FROM THE BREECH PLUG. REMOVAL OR ALTERATION WILL COMPROMISE PERFORMANCE OF THE FIREARM, CREATE AN UNSAFE SITUATION, AND VOID YOUR WARRANTY.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly, printed p.46

steps.title: Nipple and clean-out screw out of the breech plug
steps.action: Take the nipple out with the nipple wrench and the clean-out screw out with a screwdriver, and set both aside. With both out, the fire channel through the drum is open from end to end.
steps.quote: 8. From the breech plug, remove the nipple with your nipple wrench and clean out screw with a screw driver. Set aside.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly, printed p.46

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You should now have the stock with the lock and triggers still in it, the barrel, the breech plug with its drum, the nipple, the clean-out screw, the wedge, the screws and the ramrod. That is the whole disassembly Traditions publishes for the ShedHorn, and the book forbids going any further. The cleaning comes next. There is no Deep Clean for this gun because the book publishes nothing deeper.
steps.quote: DANGER: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE YOUR SHEDHORN™ ANY FURTHER THAN WHAT IS DESCRIBED IN THIS MANUAL.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly, printed p.44

steps.title: Solvent on the bronze brush, and let it sit fifteen minutes
steps.action: Put a bronze brush on the ramrod or range rod and wet it with black powder bore solvent, or use foaming bore solvent. Let it work in the barrel for fifteen minutes, but do not let it dry. Dried solvent leaves the fouling stuck on again.
steps.quote: 2. Spray a bore solvent, such as Traditions® EZClean2®, on your bronze brush. Note: Traditions® Foaming Bore Solvent can also be used instead of spraying the bore solvent on the bronze brush. Allow solvent to sit for 15 minutes inside the barrel. This will allow time for the solvent to engage and penetrate the fouling. Do not let it dry.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — Detailed Cleaning, printed p.46

steps.title: Scrub the breech plug threads and its fire channel
steps.action: Soak or spray the breech plug, then scrub the outside threads and the inside with a stiff brush, fire channel included. Push a pipe cleaner through the small passages until it comes out clean and dry. Fouling left in the threads is what seizes a plug next time.
steps.quote: Use a stiff brush to clean the outside threads and inner area of the breech plug including the fire channel. A pipe cleaner can be used to get the smaller areas clean and dry.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — Detailed Cleaning, printed p.47

steps.title: Pick the nipple clean
steps.action: Soak the nipple in the same bath or spray it inside and out, then clear its hole with the nipple pick. The flash from the cap has to get through that hole, so a partly plugged one gives you a misfire or a hangfire.
steps.quote: 4. To clean your nipple, your can drop into the same parts bath as the breech plug or spray the outside and inside with solvent. Using the nipple pick, remove any fouling.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — Detailed Cleaning, printed p.47

steps.title: Clean inside the bolster through the clean-out hole
steps.action: Spray solvent into the bolster through the hole the clean-out screw came out of and work a pipe cleaner through it. This is how the drum gets cleaned without taking it off the plug.
steps.quote: 5. Clean inside the bolster where the clean out screw was removed from. Spray solvent into the bolster area and clean this area with a pipe cleaner.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — Detailed Cleaning, printed p.47

steps.title: Brush the bore from the breech end
steps.action: With the plug out, push the brush in at the breech and out of the muzzle, then draw it back. Working from the breech pushes the fouling out of the muzzle and lets the brush scrub the whole bore.
steps.quote: 6. To clean your barrel, insert your bronze brush into the breech area. Push the ramrod from the breech to the muzzle until the brush exits the muzzle. Pull the ramrod back through the barrel towards the breech. The technique allows you to help break up fouling.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — Detailed Cleaning, printed p.47

steps.title: Dry patches until one comes out clean
steps.action: Change the brush for the cleaning jag and run dry cotton patches through the bore. Keep going until a patch comes out clean. Moisture left in a black powder bore rusts it overnight.
steps.quote: 7. Remove the bronze brush from the ramrod and attach the cleaning jag. 8. Place a dry cotton patch over the jag and insert it into the breech. Run the ramrod with the patch from the muzzle to the breech. Pull the ramrod back through to the muzzle. Repeat until patch comes out clean.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — Detailed Cleaning, printed p.47

steps.title: Season the bore and oil the outside
steps.action: Push one patch of seasoning lube or gun lube from the muzzle to the breech, then wipe a light coat of gun oil over the outside of the barrel and every metal surface. Keep it light. The book also warns against firing with excess oil or grease in the bore.
steps.quote: 9. Using a Traditions® Cleaning & Seasoning Patch or some gun lube on a dry patch, place the patch over the cleaning jag and insert into the muzzle. Push the patch from the muzzle to the breech. This will help protect against rust and allow for easier loading. 10. Apply a light coating of gun oil to the outside of the barrel and all metal surfaces.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — Detailed Cleaning, printed p.47

steps.title: Grease the nipple threads and the breech plug threads
steps.action: Grease the nipple threads, then put plenty of breech plug grease on the breech plug threads. Use breech plug grease, not whatever is on the bench. The book is plain that the wrong lubricant damages the o-ring and seizes the plug.
steps.quote: 11. Lubricate the threads of the nipple with grease. 12. Generously lubricate the threads of the breech plug with breech plug grease. Not using the recommended lubricant will cause o-ring damage and breech plug seizure.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR TRADITIONS® SHEDHORN™ — FIT-85 02-23 AKH — 19. Disassembly, Detailed Cleaning & Reassembly — Detailed Cleaning, printed p.48

deepAbsentReason: The book ends at the field strip. Its DISASSEMBLY section stops with the nipple and clean-out screw out of the breech plug ("Your firearm is now disassembled.", printed p.46), and the same section forbids going further: "DO NOT DISASSEMBLE YOUR SHEDHORN™ ANY FURTHER THAN WHAT IS DESCRIBED IN THIS MANUAL." (printed p.44). The book publishes no procedure for taking the lock or the triggers out of the stock. The lock and trigger parts lists (pp.19-20) are reference diagrams only, and the book forbids taking the bolster drum off the breech plug (p.46).

cleaning.name: Bore
tasks: Wet a bronze brush with black powder bore solvent and let it sit 15 minutes. Do not let it dry
Brush from the breech end out through the muzzle and back
Run dry cotton patches until one comes out clean
Push one seasoning or gun-lube patch from muzzle to breech
No excess oil or grease left in the bore before firing

cleaning.name: Breech plug and ignition
tasks: Scrub the breech plug threads and inside with a stiff brush, fire channel included
Pipe-cleaner the small passages until clean and dry
Clean inside the bolster through the clean-out screw hole. The bolster drum stays on the plug
Grease the nipple threads, and put plenty of breech plug grease on the breech plug threads

cleaning.name: Metalwork
tasks: Light coat of gun oil on the outside of the barrel and all metal surfaces
Check the breech plug o-ring for wear when the plug comes out

cleaning.name: Storage
tasks: Store uncharged and unprimed, cool, dry and locked
Not in a gun case, which can speed up condensation and corrosion
During long storage, check the bore and outside for pitting and rust

reassembly: Put the clean-out screw back in the bolster and the nipple back in the breech plug. Do not overtighten either, and do not cross-thread the nipple.

Look through the breech plug's fire channel to make sure it is clear, grease its threads, then thread it into the barrel clockwise by hand until it seats firmly, lined up with the timing mark on the barrel. If it will not thread smoothly or seat fully, take it out and check the o-ring and both sets of threads for fouling.

Start both lock plate screws but do not tighten them. Put the forward screw through the loop of the ramrod retaining spring, with the curled end pointing back toward the buttstock and the curved belly side facing down onto the ramrod.
Set the tang in its place in the stock without tightening the tang screw.
Put the breech plug end of the barrel into the tang and lower the barrel into the stock channel until it is fully seated. You should be able to see clearly through the wedge slot.
Tighten the tang screw, then tighten the front and rear lock plate screws without overtightening.
Drive the barrel wedge back in from the lock plate side with the tenon lined up so you can see through it. If it does not go in easily, do not force it.
Return the ramrod to the thimbles.
fncheck: With the gun empty, uncapped and pointed somewhere safe, put the hammer on half cock and set the rear trigger. Pressing the front trigger or pushing the hammer forward must not make the hammer fall. Then bring the hammer to full cock, set the rear trigger, and push forward on the hammer. It must stay put. The triggers are set at the factory and are not adjustable. If the lock or triggers do not behave this way, stop and contact Traditions. The book also says never to dry fire the gun.
